Earlier this year, rumors were swirling that iOS 26.4 would introduce a revamped Health app. The project was subsequently delayed, and after iOS 27 launched, it too came and went without this overhaul ever appearing.

With the next-generation Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 arriving next month, it's worth asking: will these new features debut alongside the new hardware?

Precedent

First, it's worth explaining why these features are likely to arrive in September. You might be thinking, "Shouldn't all software be unveiled in June?" But the truth is, there is precedent for this.

watchOS 9's Low Power Mode, watchOS 11's sleep apnea detection, and watchOS 26's hypertension notifications were all features unveiled in September, even though they didn't require the latest hardware to function.

For these reasons, even if the latest Health app upgrades don't necessarily require a brand-new Apple Watch, it's quite possible that Apple will wait until September to officially unveil them.

There's Still Time

Before WWDC27, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman warned that the new Health app upgrades (codenamed Project Mulberry) might not appear at the WWDC keynote. That prediction proved accurate:

Does this mean Project Mulberry will definitely appear at the September keynote? Not necessarily. However, given the multiple precedents of new features being unveiled in September, plus the fact that we already know it might launch slightly later than WWDC, a September debut still seems quite possible—even if it ultimately arrives in October alongside iOS 27.1.

Feature Recap

Rumors about these features have been constantly shifting, because there are too many variables involved. You may have heard that one of the ideas was to launch a standalone Health+ service, complete with videos featuring doctors providing explanations. However, reports indicate those plans have been scaled back, with the features instead being folded into the existing Health app experience.

Two things are fairly clear, however: first, an AI health coach will be added to offer recommendations using your Health app data; second, the camera will be used to provide real-time guidance for fitness and other health-related activities. Another key focus of this upgrade is a brand-new design for the Health app, making it easier for you to understand all the data.

Beyond that, we can only wait and see. Personally, I'm quite looking forward to having a better way to organize and understand my Apple health data.
